newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Wall St seen boosting S.African shares next week.
newsitem.headline: Wall St seen boosting S.African shares next week.

text.p: South African shares were seen stronger next week with portfolio managers and dealers saying there was a firm undertone to the market, helped by continued gains on Wall Street.

But trading was expected to be thin. The market will close early on Tuesday ahead of the New Year's Day holiday on Wednesday. Many players were on holiday and were not expected to return until January 6.
"I think it will be strong...Wall Street is flying and we are doing nothing. But I think it will be okay next week," said a portfolio manager who declined to be identified.
Players may try and push the market higher ahead of the close of unit trusts' fourth quarter on Tuesday.

However, there was unlikely to be extensive window-dressing. "Most people are away. They have done their positioning and gone on leave, hoping no one would fiddle with their prices," said Andre Joubert a portfolio manager at Investec Asset Management.
"The JET system has put a stop to funny prices...There will not be a big turn next week, it has been quite a poor year for unit trusts," Joubert told Reuters.
Gold shares, which traded flat this week, were again seen static with the exception of stocks heavily weighted in unit trust portfolios.
In the absence of company results next week, the equity market will be looking for direction from key money supply and credit extension data due out on Thursday.
A Reuters forecast of economists revealed expectations that money supply growth will slow to between 14.4 percent and 16.3 percent with the consensus at 15.5 percent from 15.96 percent previously.
Private credit extension was also seen edging lower to a range between 17.5 percent and 18.6 percent with consensus at 18.2 percent from 18.86 percent.
